gloss: to take on; to shoulder; to burden oneself with

definitions.gloss: to take on; to shoulder; to burden oneself with
definitions.explanation: To take on a heavy responsibility, burden, or problem — often more than one should or can handle. A compound verb formed from 背負う (to carry on one's back) + 込む (into/deeply). Almost always used figuratively for emotional, financial, or social burdens.

examples.japanese: {一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}{背負|せお}い{込|こ}まないで。
examples.english: Don't take everything on by yourself.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{多額|たがく}の{借金|しゃっきん}を{背負|せお}い{込|こ}んでしまった。
examples.english: He ended up saddled with a large debt.

examples.japanese: {責任感|せきにんかん}が{強|つよ}い{人|ひと}ほど、{問題|もんだい}を{背負|せお}い{込|こ}みやすい。
examples.english: The stronger one's sense of responsibility, the more likely they are to burden themselves with problems.

notes:
USAGE:
{背負|せお}い{込|こ}む implies an excessive or overwhelming burden, often self-imposed. It is frequently used with {一人|ひとり}で (by oneself) to describe someone who tries to handle everything alone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一人|ひとり}で{背負|せお}い{込|こ}む (take it all on alone)
- {借金|しゃっきん}を{背負|せお}い{込|こ}む (be saddled with debt)
- {責任|せきにん}を{背負|せお}い{込|こ}む (shoulder responsibility)
- {悩|なや}みを{背負|せお}い{込|こ}む (burden oneself with worries)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{背負|せお}う means "to carry on one's back" and can be either literal or figurative. {背負|せお}い{込|こ}む adds the nuance of taking on too much or getting deeply burdened. {抱|かか}え{込|こ}む also means "to take on" problems but implies holding them close rather than carrying them on one's back.
